schema.targets.<key>: classifier: model, candidates, cv_metrics, test_metrics (+95% bootstrap CI over students), logistic_test_metrics, baselines, gain_over_success_score, threshold, calibration, ablation, by_semester, by_department, early_detection, fairness_out_of_sample, prevalence
schema.regression: next-semester SGPA: model, test_metrics, baselines, prediction_interval80
schema.threshold: a calibrated probability at or above it counts as at-risk; tuned for recall >= 0.85 on out-of-fold training predictions (brief requires 0.80)
schema.positive class: at-risk; for placement it is NOT ready, so probability of being ready = 1 - probability

caveats: The data is synthetic: every student, mark and outcome was generated from rules we designed (see data/DATASET.md).
Metrics therefore demonstrate that the pipeline is leakage-free and works end to end; they are not a claim about accuracy on real students.
The test set (20% of students) was used exactly once, after every modelling choice was fixed.
Retrain on the institution's own records before any decision is based on these predictions.
generated_at: deterministic (no wall-clock time is stored so outputs are reproducible)

split.rule: students, not rows, are split; test touched once

sgpa_below_6.title: Semester performance: SGPA below 6

model.chosen_because: logistic regression: boosting did not beat it by >= 0.01 cv-AUC, so the simpler, explainable model is used

sgpa_below_6.threshold_rule: best precision among thresholds with recall >= 0.85 on out-of-fold calibrated probabilities (the brief requires >= 0.80; the extra 0.05 is a safety margin for sampling noise on held-out students)

ablation.note: Same model family and parameters, trained WITHOUT success_score_proxy and round1_risk_flag.

early_detection.definition: Held-out rows that became at-risk although the Round 1 flag was Low at the cut-off.

global_drivers.method: permutation importance on held-out students, 20 repeats, scoring=roc_auc

sgpa_below_6.drivers_explain: logistic model (the forecast itself uses the same model)

explanation_faithfulness.check: for 200 random rows per target: |sum of per-feature contributions + intercept - logistic decision function|
explanation_faithfulness.driver_display_rule: Per-student drivers are the largest family-level effects that also agree with common-sense direction (higher attendance means lower risk, more backlogs means higher risk). Effects that run against it come from offsets between correlated measures; they stay inside the probability but are not shown as reasons.
